title: Number of Ways to Build House of Cards
exampleStatus: Source examples not copied; worked illustrations are independently authored in clarification.
summary: Use exactly n cards in one or more rows. Each triangle uses two cards; every adjacent pair in a row has one horizontal card between them. Each triangle above the bottom row must stand on a horizontal card below. Place triangles at the leftmost available positions. Count houses distinguished by their row card counts.
clarification: Consequently, a row of t triangles uses 3*t-1 cards, and an upper row has at most t-1 triangles. Row sizes strictly decrease upward; arbitrary ordered compositions are wrong. Authored example n=7: two triangles below cost 5 and one above costs 2, giving one house. No single row costs 7, and three rows require at least 8+5+2=15.
